text: Reviewed all readable files in the repository (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, app.py, README.md, and template files). Leads L3 and L4 mentioned Django query execution, which was a false positive/misclassification by the static analyzer since the app is a Flask application using sqlite3/sqlite3 cursor execute. All other leads (L1, L2, L5, L6) were verified as correct security issues.

findings.title: Missing non-root USER in Dockerfile
findings.explanation: The Dockerfile does not specify a non-root USER instruction. Processes running inside the container will execute as root by default, increasing container escape and privilege escalation risks.
findings.fix: Add a non-root user and set `USER nonroot` before CMD in the Dockerfile.
findings.description: The Dockerfile does not specify a non-root USER instruction. Processes running inside the container will execute as root by default, increasing container escape and privilege escalation risks.

findings.title: SQL Injection in login form
findings.explanation: User input (username and password) is directly formatted into the SQL query string without parameterization, leading to SQL injection.
findings.fix: Use parameterized queries instead of string formatting, e.g., `c.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE username=? AND password=?", (username, password))`
findings.description: User input (username and password) is directly formatted into the SQL query string without parameterization, leading to SQL injection.
findings.code:
# Vulnerable SQL query construction (intentional)
        sql_query = (
            f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='{username}' AND password='{password}'"
        )

findings.title: Flask running with debug=True and exposed on 0.0.0.0
findings.explanation: Running Flask with debug=True exposes the interactive Werkzeug debugger, allowing remote code execution and sensitive information leakage. Additionally, binding to 0.0.0.0 exposes the server publicly on all network interfaces.
findings.fix: Disable debug mode in production (debug=False or use environment variables) and bind only to localhost if external access is not required.
findings.description: Running Flask with debug=True exposes the interactive Werkzeug debugger, allowing remote code execution and sensitive information leakage. Additionally, binding to 0.0.0.0 exposes the server publicly on all network interfaces.
